newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government says Tshisekedi verges on treason.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government says Tshisekedi verges on treason.

text.p: Zaire's government said on Friday that radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi had come close to treason after he declared himself willing to negotiate with rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
"These irresponsible statements verge on treason and complicity with the enemy," government spokesman Boguo Makeli said in a televised account of Friday's cabinet meeting.
Boguo said Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UPDS) was the only Zairean political party with its flag flying in rebel-held territory.

The government, he added, had seized from the civil and military judicial authorities information in their possession concerning Tshisekedi's party and "Rwandan acts of aggression against Zaire" so as to establish responsibility.
He said the rebels, whom he accused of being Rwandan-backed, had compensated Tshisekedi's party for its help by allowing it to control certain towns in the east including Goma and Uvira.

Earlier, Tshisekedi told Radio France Internationale that President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is in southern France recuperating from cancer surgery, had given him a mandate to form a national unity government. He met Mobutu on Thursday.
Mobutu's spokesman in Kinshasa, Professor Kabuya Lumuna, expressed astonishment at the idea and said it was unfounded.
Tshisekedi described the revolt in the east as an internal problem and played down Rwandan involvement. He said dialogue was the only solution with a role in Zaire for Kabila.
